imageDirection.concreteScene: Interior of Jay's Oakland shop late at night, viewed from just inside the door, past the short queue, toward the register. Jay stands behind the counter with the shop phone lying face down and a small bagged bottle pushed toward Tan. Tan faces him on the customer side, her hand just withdrawn from over the counter. Two locals wait behind her with ordinary purchases, one holding a six-pack.
imageDirection.factLeftToImage: What the shop actually is: how a visitor-facing refit sits on top of years of working wear, how the queue arranges itself in the narrow space, and who is looking at whom in the moment after the failed payment. The prose does not describe the room or the distribution of attention; the plate supplies both.
mustRemain: Jay is behind the counter and Tan is on the customer side, with two customers in line behind her, one holding a six-pack.
The shop phone lies face down on the counter and the clef is a single slim bottle already inside a bag, unpaid for.
Jay and Tan both read as ordinary young people in ordinary clothes; neither is styled as a glamorous science-fiction figure.
imageDirection.narrativeJob: Fix Jay and Tan as the two people this book will keep returning to, and establish the shop as a local business partly refitted for visitor money, with attention distributed unequally around Tan's failure at the counter.
purposefulChanges: This is the book's first plate, so it introduces Jay, Tan, and the shop interior rather than revising an earlier image.
The moment shown is the beat after the transaction has been abandoned: the phone is already face down and the gift already sits on the counter between them.
unresolvedFacts: Clef's contents, color, and labeling beyond being a small cold bottle from the case behind the counter.
Tan's origin should register only as small wrong notes in dress and bearing, not as visible future technology on her body.
The shop's name, full stock, and the street outside the counter area.

imageDirection.concreteScene: The crowded back room of a bar at night: a small low stage with a four-piece band, trumpet player, upright bassist, drummer, and guitarist, under warm house light. In the middle of the standing crowd, Jay and Tan stand close together, her back against his chest, his arm around her waist, both turned toward the stage and visibly enjoying the music. Near the wall by the door, apart from the crowd, a neatly dressed stranger holds a small handheld device raised slightly toward the stage, an ordinary unremarkable object, their attention on the band rather than on anyone in the room. The view is from behind and to one side of the crowd, so that Jay, Tan, the band, and the stranger at the edge are all legible.
imageDirection.factLeftToImage: That the performance is being recorded tonight by a visitor at the edge of the room, unnoticed by Jay and Tan. The prose establishes that a recording of this music exists and sells at Tan's home coordinate; only the image shows a recording being made.
mustRemain: Jay as the young man from the shop plate: dark curly hair, dark hooded jacket, watchful expression.
Tan as the woman from the shop plate: dark hair tied back, loose gray-green jacket over plain clothes.
Jay and Tan physically at ease with each other, together in the crowd as companions.
An ordinary 2025 Oakland interior with worn material detail; no glowing, futuristic, or supernatural visual effects anywhere, including on the recording device.
imageDirection.narrativeJob: Show that the music Jay and Tan are enjoying is being taken down tonight, connecting the uncredited compilation Tan owns to a plausible source in this very room, while the couple remains inside the pleasure of the performance and does not see it happening.
purposefulChanges: The setting moves from Jay's shop counter to a live music venue at night.
Jay and Tan are no longer separated by a counter; they stand together in the crowd, touching.
A third significant figure appears: the stranger by the door making a recording with a small handheld device, an act as ordinary as anyone holding up a phone.
unresolvedFacts: Whether the stranger is the source of Tan's compilation or connected to any company.
The stranger's identity, era of origin, and face in any detail.
The exact workings of the recording device beyond being a small ordinary handheld object.
The identities and futures of the band members.

copyedits.reason: Remove one unmatched provider-added terminal quotation mark.
Correct dialogue punctuation without changing wording.

imageDirection.concreteScene: The cramped back room of Jay's shop at night: a small break table between a microwave and stacked register-tape boxes, an open aluminum case, and three printed chart sheets squared under a clear film overlay with one continuous route line crossing all three. Tan stands over the table with one hand flat on the film, mid-explanation; Jay leans in close, thumb near the route line. The view is from above Jay's shoulder, angled so the chart surface fills the lower half of the frame and stays readable, drawn like a hydrographic current chart with flow lines, stamped revision marks, gray confidence shading, and dense pencil annotation crowding the printed lanes at the margins.
imageDirection.factLeftToImage: How the route physically reads: the relative extent of the printed, company-stamped lanes versus the handwritten traded observations in the margins; how much of the chart sits under gray low-confidence shading, especially around the Phantas correction; and how visibly dated and provisional the revision stamps make the sheets appear.
mustRemain: Jay and Tan match their prior appearances: Jay a young dark-haired man in dark work clothes, Tan with dark hair tied back and a loose jacket.
The map is paper and clear film on an ordinary table, printed in the manner of a nautical current chart, not a glowing screen, projection, or futuristic interface.
The setting is the working back room of the same modest 2025 Oakland shop, cluttered and functional, lit by ordinary fixtures.
Three distinct chart sheets, one per temporal axis, with a single route crossing all three under the film overlay.
imageDirection.narrativeJob: Shows the reader what Jay is actually being asked to trust: a physical navigational chart whose printed corporate lanes, hand-traded margin observations, revision stamps, and gray low-confidence zones make the difficulty of temporal travel and the unequal ownership of its knowledge legible at a glance, while keeping the moment a quiet working scene between two people at a break table.
purposefulChanges: First scene set in the shop's back room rather than at the counter; Tan is instructing rather than buying.
Jay and Tan stand shoulder to shoulder over shared work, a working closeness replacing the customer and clerk arrangement of the first plate.
unresolvedFacts: The name and emblem of the PRMTT company stay indistinct; its mark should read as a repeated official stamp without legible branding.
The chart's notation stays suggestive rather than fully legible; no readable dates, coordinates, or invented equations.
Jay's decision about making the crossing is not settled; his posture is study, not agreement.
Whatever lies at the destination end of the route stays unshown.

imageDirection.concreteScene: Night at the Lagos lagoon ferry terminal, seen from within the small crowd of off-shift crews, close enough that the chalked lines are legible. On the terminal wall beside the fare notice and the departure board of outer lagoon stops: three hand-drawn current traces in different hands that visibly disagree at one crossing point, with witnessed names, observation times, and the return order chalked beneath the first. Eniola stands at the wall holding chalk and a folded timetable. Wale, a terminal officer, reads from a printed order. Balogun copies the wall into a paper sounding book; Chidi photographs it with a borrowed phone. Behind them at the berth, the ferry sits with its console dark and its mirror array folded, lagoon water and distant stop lamps beyond.
imageDirection.factLeftToImage: The scale of dissemination and dependence that the prose does not enumerate: how many crews are actually recording the wall into their own books, and the departure board tying the disputed crossing to the named outer stops whose morning runs will follow one trace or another.
mustRemain: Eniola Akinyemi is the same navigator who walked the deck recording witnesses in the prior folio, now on the terminal side of the berth without her ferry.

The first chalked trace shows the licensed line, her corrected line, the return order, and the witnessed names and times from the crossing, matching the sounding-book record made with Balogun, Chidi, and Mrs. Adeyemi.
Balogun and Chidi are working crew in ordinary ferry clothes; records are kept on paper in witnessed hand, with one phone photograph as the exception.
The ferry is an ordinary lagoon vessel fitted with mirrors and a heat exchanger; its console is locked and dark, not damaged or destroyed.
Nothing supernatural or fantastical marks the temporal traffic; the traces are chart lines with times, like current soundings.
imageDirection.narrativeJob: The map has moved from a licensed console and a single sounding book onto a public wall carrying at least three materially incompatible traces in different hands.
purposefulChanges: The map has moved from a licensed console and a single sounding book onto a public wall carrying at least three materially incompatible traces in different hands.
Eniola is suspended: she stands among the crews rather than at the helm, and the ferry behind her is closed to her.
The audience has changed from eleven passengers to other working crews who are copying and recording, not merely watching.
unresolvedFacts: Which of the three traces is correct at the crossing point.
The wall must not appear erased or partly cleaned; this is the moment while the order is being read and the copying is still underway.
The company's name, logo, and uniform details stay unspecified.
Whether Mrs. Adeyemi is still present; do not place her in the scene.
The readable text of the suspension order beyond the fact that it is a printed order.
What consequences Wale or the company will pursue next.
